ledger.claim: The governed measurement of this trip is the GPS trace: 22.400 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against a booked optimal of 13.0 km. That is an excess of 9.4 km, or 72.3% of optimal, so both POL-RD-01 gates — more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute — are passed several times over and a route deviation is ESTABLISHED. Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs and the rounded trip_record copy (22.4 km) is not the field to test the threshold on; here they agree, so the result is the same either way.

The trace cannot be attacked as incomplete: 177 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps in the gaps array, a largest inter-fix straight-line step of 177.9 m and a maximum interval of 10 seconds. That is below the 500 m jump limb and far below the 90-second gap and 30-second cadence limbs of POL-RD-07, so the trace is NOT impaired for policy purposes, the deviation may be established on the trace alone without independent corroboration, and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is not engaged.

Even taking the driver's closure defence at its highest, POL-RD-03 does not exonerate the whole detour — it caps exoneration. The justified excess is min(measured 9.4 km, 1.30 x (shortest lawful alternative 15.2 km - booked optimal 13.0 km) + 1.00) = min(9.4, 3.86) = 3.86 km, giving a closure-adjusted optimal of 16.86 km. The remaining 5.54 km of excess is beyond the cap, is therefore not exonerated, and is refundable under POL-RD-02 computed against that adjusted optimal route rather than the booked one. The excess remaining (5.54 km) still exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km, so the deviation stands even after the adjustment.

The closure is a weak explanation for a 22.400 km drive. The LTA advisory the driver relies on itself records a shortest lawful alternative of 15.2 km between the same endpoints, so an alternative-route detour should have added roughly 2.2 km — yet the vehicle covered 22.400 km, some 7.2 km beyond even that alternative. The 3.86 km cap in POL-RD-03 is the outer limit of exoneration; the balance of the excess is unexplained by the closure and stays with the driver.

None of the excess can be pinned on the rider. The chat log for this trip carries exactly two messages — the driver's 'Reached AMK Hub taxi stand, silver Prius' and the rider's 'ok coming down' — and neither carries a waypoint_hint nor names a road or place. The POL-RD-04 test (rider instruction, timestamped before the corridor was left, specific enough to act on, corroborated by the trace) is unavailable, no distance is excluded on that ground, and under POL-RD-14 an unevidenced instruction causes nothing.

The refund route is open because this is a metered trip. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 (upfront-quoted fares) does not apply and the distance-and-time recomputation under POL-RD-02 is available. The ledger shows charged_total 29.52, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider is still carrying the full disputed amount today.

The arithmetic is not discretionary. Running POL-RD-02 on the closure-adjusted optimal: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 16.86 + 0.28 x 22.0) x the 1.0 surge_multiplier read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 23.405 recomputed fare. Charged_total 29.52 less 23.405 = 6.115, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 6.15 payable. That is above the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor and well short of the 90% full-refund share, so the rider is owed a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.15 rather than the SGD 12.00 claimed.

Nothing is added on top of that figure and nothing is double-counted. The fare carries no ERP or toll lines (erp_lines total 0.00), no airport surcharge — correctly, since this trip does not originate at an airport — and no waiting-time fee, so no pass-through correction under POL-RD-09 arises and the POL-RD-09(1) anti-double-count rule bites: the distance-and-time refund already comprehends everything the rider is owed.

The rider's own record does not raise any extra corroboration hurdle. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4-claim gate in POL-RD-08, and the measured excess is 72.3% — far above the 30% level at which that clause could even be considered. The claim therefore needs nothing beyond the trace, and no other field on either profile may carry a finding under POL-GEN-01.

In the alternative, if the tribunal declines to apply the POL-RD-03 cap because limb (c) is not made out on this record — the derived closure block leaves intersects_route and road_name null, and no artifact shows the trace leaving the optimal corridor before the closed CTE city tunnel segment and rejoining after — then the driver has not discharged the burden POL-RD-08 places on him, the whole 9.4 km excess stands, and POL-RD-02 against the booked optimal yields ((3.80 + 0.75 x 13.0 + 0.28 x 17) x 1.0) + 0.80 = 19.11, a refund of 10.41 rounded up to SGD 10.45.

The excess as measured is not in dispute and is taken from the trace, as POL-RD-01 requires: the trace polyline between the recorded pickup and dropoff is 22.40 km against a booked optimal of 13.0 km, an excess of 9.4 km or 72.3% of optimal. The governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km; trip_record.actual_distance_km is only a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and is not cited for the threshold test.

The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 177 fixes over the trip at a 10 s cadence, the largest interval between consecutive fixes is 10 s and there are no gaps at all, the largest straight-line step is 177.9 m (far under the 500 m jump limb) and no sampling interval exceeds 30 s. No limb (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so the deviation needs no independent corroboration and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged.

The LTA notice EV-ADVIS-04002-01 closes the CTE city tunnel between the Bukit Timah Road entrance and the Chin Swee Road exit, all lanes, for tunnel maintenance — exactly the segment the booked optimal route traverses, as the trip record's route_planned event records the booking route as 'CTE southbound through the city tunnel, Chin Swee Rd exit, Outram Rd'. The advisory limb (a) of POL-RD-03 is therefore satisfied on the face of the two artifacts.

The validity window limb (b) of POL-RD-03 is satisfied: the advisory runs from 2026-09-05T23:30 to 2026-09-06T05:00 and the trace runs from 00:40:30 to 01:09:49 on 2026-09-06, so the vehicle would have reached the closed city-tunnel segment early in the trip, comfortably inside the window even before the 15-minute buffer POL-RD-03 allows at each end.

The actual-route limb (c) of POL-RD-03 is satisfied on the record: the driver's statement on file is that he took PIE and then the AYE to Outram, which leaves the CTE corridor before the closed segment and rejoins it at the Outram end rather than driving through the closure. The advisory itself states a shortest lawful alternative of 15.2 km between the booked endpoints, and a 22.40 km actual route is consistent with a driver who went around the closure rather than through it.

Exoneration under POL-RD-03 is capped and the driver claims no more than the cap: the justified excess is the lesser of the measured 9.4 km and 1.30 x (15.2 - 13.0) + 1.00 = 3.86 km. Only 3.86 km of the 9.4 km is excused, and the remaining 5.54 km stands against the driver, which is why the outcome here is a partial refund and not NO_ACTION.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider showed an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace, so the burden shifted to the driver; the driver discharges it the way the clause demands, by pointing to a specific artifact (the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-04002-01) and a specific exculpatory clause (POL-RD-03), not by a general assertion that traffic was bad.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run against the closure-adjusted optimal rather than the booked one, as POL-RD-03 requires and as the METERED fare model on the fare_breakdown permits. The adjusted optimal is 13.0 + 3.86 = 16.86 km with duration 22.0 min scaled from the booked 17 min, giving recomputed_fare = 3.80 + 0.75 x 16.86 + 0.28 x 22.0 + 0.80 = 23.405; refund = 29.52 - 23.405 = 6.115, rounded up to 6.15. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 6.15, not the 12.00 the rider claims and not the 10.45 the unadjusted 13.0 km route would produce.

POL-RD-01 requires materiality to be assessed on the excess remaining after the POL-RD-03 adjustment, not on the excess as first measured: 9.4 - 3.86 = 5.54 km, which is about 32.9% of the adjusted optimal of 16.86 km and is below both the 50% and the 8.0 km materiality gates. The deviation is therefore established but not material, and the POL-RD-06 FULL_REFUND uplift in limb (b) is not engaged.

Even if the deviation were treated as material, the driver profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 310, so no repeat pattern is established under POL-RD-06 and neither the full-refund uplift nor the conduct referral follows from this trip. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter of 1 is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names.

ledger.claim: The fare ledger carries ERP and tolls of 0.00 with no gantry lines at all and no airport surcharge line, so there is no off-route or phantom pass-through to correct. Under POL-RD-09(2) the distance and time charges stand because the closure was an external event the driver did not cause, and nothing is added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and the case should be decided rather than escalated: the trip identifier matches across the trip record, the trace and the fare ledger; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07; the pickup, start and end timestamps agree across the artifacts; the exculpatory clause the driver invokes is backed by an advisory that is in the pool, covers the trip window and carries the field POL-RD-03 needs; and the refund of 6.15 is far below both the SGD 150.00 ceiling and charged_total.

This is not the missing-advisory case POL-RD-13 was written for. The traffic advisory is on file for this trip — admissibility status COMPLETE, weight 1.0, every payload field populated, including the shortest lawful alternative of 15.2 km — so POL-RD-03 is available and the driver's asserted traffic cause is tested against a real advisory and passes. POL-RD-13(2), which discards an uncited traffic excuse, does not strip the exoneration away.

On the chat log the driver does not overreach: it holds two messages, the driver's arrival notice at the AMK Hub taxi stand and the rider's 'ok coming down', neither of which is a rider instruction to detour and neither of which carries a waypoint_hint. POL-RD-04 therefore excludes no distance from the excess, and the driver makes no claim of a rider-requested detour — the exoneration in this case rests on POL-RD-03 alone.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this was a metered ride from Ang Mo Kio Hub to Outram Park on 6 Sep 2026. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-04002, weight 1.0, unimpaired: 177 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, largest step 177.9 m) measures the trip at 22.40 km against the booked optimal of 13.0 km (EV-TRIP-04002). That is an excess of 9.4 km, 72.3% of optimal, so under POL-RD-01 a route deviation is established; the trace figure governs and the rounded trip-record copy agrees with it.

The driver's closure explanation is backed by a genuine artifact, not a bare assertion: LTA notice EV-ADVIS-04002-01 (weight 1.0) closes the CTE between the Bukit Timah Road entrance and the Chin Swee Road exit, all lanes, from 23:30 on 5 Sep to 05:00 on 6 Sep — the exact segment the booked route uses (the trip record's route_planned event) and inside the period the trace shows the vehicle reaching the city. That engages POL-RD-03, but the clause caps how far 'there was a closure' reaches: the shortest lawful alternative was 15.2 km, so the justified excess is 1.30 x (15.2 - 13.0) + 1.0 = 3.86 km, not the full 9.4 km. The rider's alternative argument that limb (c) is unmade because the derived block leaves intersects_route null is rejected: the trace is admitted and unimpaired, the endpoints are the same, and the closure artifact the clause reads is present, complete and covers the window, so the exoneration runs at the cap.

Because 3.86 km of the excess is excused, POL-RD-02 is recomputed against the closure-adjusted optimal: distance 13.0 + 3.86 = 16.86 km, duration 22.0 min (the booked 17 min scaled), giving a fare of 3.80 + 0.75 x 16.86 + 0.28 x 22.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 23.405. You were charged 29.52 (EV-FARE-04002, METERED). Refund = 29.52 - 23.405 = 6.115, rounded up to SGD 6.15. That is above the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor and well under the 90% full-refund share. The rider's claim of 12.00 is not supported, and the alternative figure of 10.45 is not payable because the closure exoneration does apply.

The unexcused balance is 5.54 km, about 32.9% of the adjusted optimal. It stays above the 20% establishment gate so the deviation stands, but it is below the 50% and 8.0 km materiality gates, so the deviation is not MATERIAL and the POL-RD-06 full-refund uplift and conduct referral are not engaged — the driver's profile shows no trailing-90-day pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 310), and lifetime counters such as prior_deviation_flags are context only under POL-GEN-01.

Nothing is added on top of the refund. The fare carries no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge (correctly, since the trip does not originate at an airport), so no POL-RD-09 pass-through correction arises and the anti-double-count rule bites. The chat log (EV-CHAT-04002) holds no rider detour instruction — no waypoint_hint, no road named — so POL-RD-04 excludes no distance and no driver compensation is payable. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired, the timestamps agree, the cited advisory is in the pool, and the refund is far below both the SGD 150.00 ceiling and charged_total, so the case is decided rather than escalated and there is no clause-mandated referral. The monetary effect (SGD 6.15) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic execution threshold and executes on issue. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
